questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “memory” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A first encounter with a pathogen leaves behind a population of long-lived cells specific to it. Those cells do nothing while the pathogen is absent, but on a second encounter they divide and produce antibody within days rather than the weeks the first response took. Immunological <u>memory</u> is what a vaccine is designed to establish without the illness that would otherwise establish it.

choices.label: A
choices.content: An account of past events written by a participant.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The faculty by which past events are recalled.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A capacity to respond more rapidly to something met before.

choices.label: D
choices.content: A device in which data are stored.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

questions.passage: An individual householder cannot say whether a fire will reach him, and the loss if it does may exceed everything he owns. An insurer writing ten thousand such houses cannot say either, but the proportion of them that burns in a year varies very little from one year to the next. The business rests on the fact that an event unpredictable singly becomes _____ in the aggregate.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A purified protein taken from a pathogen is far safer to inject than the whole organism and much less effective: the immune system meets it, finds nothing else amiss, and mounts little response. <u>Substances called adjuvants are added to such vaccines to produce a small local disturbance at the injection site, which draws in the cells that carry the protein to the rest of the system.</u> Aluminium salts have served this purpose since the 1920s, and the mechanism is still not fully understood.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It introduces the remedy for the shortcoming described in the preceding sentence.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It restates the preceding sentence in more technical language.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It concedes that purified proteins cannot be used in vaccines.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It gives an example of a pathogen against which vaccination has failed.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Milman Parry had argued from the Greek text alone that the recurring descriptive tags of the Iliad were a poet's tools rather than his ornaments. In the 1930s he and Albert Lord took recording equipment into rural Yugoslavia and worked with singers who could perform epics of many thousands of lines without any written text. Those singers proved to use the same phrase in the same metrical position again and again, and no two performances of one song by one singer were identical.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To argue that the Yugoslav epics are older than the Greek ones.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.content: To describe the recording equipment available in the 1930s.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To describe how a claim about an ancient text was tested against a living practice.

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A vine of the Cuban rainforest opens flowers whose nectar is taken almost entirely by bats. Above each flower stands a dish-shaped leaf, concave and unusually stiff, which returns a strong echo from a wide range of directions instead of the narrow one an ordinary leaf reflects. Bats trained to find a feeder among artificial foliage located it in about half the time when a similar dish was fixed above it. The plant appears to advertise in the medium its pollinators use.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The nectar of the vine is richer than that of related species.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Stiff leaves reflect less sound than flexible ones.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A plant's leaf is shaped so as to be conspicuous to pollinators that navigate by echo.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Bats find flowers more easily at night than during the day.

questions.stem: According to the text, why is a tool reheated after quenching?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Steel quenched from red heat into water comes out very hard and so brittle that a file will chip it and a blow will snap it. The structure formed by the sudden cooling is strained internally, and reheating the piece to a few hundred degrees lets part of that strain relax. The result is a little softer than the quenched steel and far less liable to break, which is why an edge tool is always tempered after hardening and never used straight from the quench.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To allow a file to cut it during the final shaping.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To make it harder than quenching alone can make it.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To relieve internal strain at the cost of a little hardness.

choices.label: D
choices.content: To restore a shape lost during the sudden cooling.

MeasureTimetable ruleHolding rule

questions.stem: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the conclusion that the groyne redistributed sand rather than adding to the shore as a whole?

questions.passage: Current sent along a land telegraph line weakens with distance, and beyond a few hundred kilometres the receiving instrument no longer moves reliably. questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

questions.passage: Sulphide minerals sit unaltered in a coal or metal deposit for as long as they are out of contact with air. Working the deposit exposes fresh sulphide surfaces in the roadways and in the waste heaps, and the pumping that keeps the workings dry admits air to them as well. When a mine closes and the pumps are stopped, water rises through those roadways and finds its way to the surface, so a closure is likely to be followed by _____

questions.stem: The student wants to explain how the heat-sensitive square changed what happens after a refrigerator failure. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Most vaccines lose potency if they are allowed to freeze or to rise above about eight degrees Celsius.
  • A dose that has lost potency looks exactly like one that has not.
  • Vials can carry a small square of heat-sensitive material that darkens irreversibly with cumulative exposure.
  • A health worker compares the square with a printed reference ring before giving the dose.
  • Millions of doses used to be discarded on suspicion after a refrigerator failure.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Because a spoiled dose is indistinguishable by eye from a sound one, a square that darkens with cumulative heat lets a worker keep the vials that are still good instead of discarding a whole batch on suspicion.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Vials can carry a small square of heat-sensitive material that darkens irreversibly with cumulative exposure.

choices.label: C
choices.content: A health worker compares the square with a printed reference ring before giving the dose.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Most vaccines lose potency if they are allowed to freeze or to rise above about eight degrees Celsius.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the shield succeeded where the earlier attempts under the river had failed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • Marc Brunel watched a shipworm bore through timber behind a shell it pushed ahead of itself.
  • He patented a tunnelling shield in 1818: an iron frame divided into cells in which miners worked at the face.
  • The frame was pushed forward by screws and brickwork was built up immediately behind it.
  • The Thames Tunnel, driven with the shield, opened in 1843.
  • Earlier attempts to tunnel under the Thames had all been abandoned when the river broke in.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Marc Brunel watched a shipworm bore through timber behind a shell it pushed ahead of itself.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The Thames Tunnel, driven with the shield, opened in 1843.

choices.label: C
choices.content: He patented a tunnelling shield in 1818: an iron frame divided into cells in which miners worked at the face.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Because the iron frame held the ground at the face while brickwork closed up immediately behind it, no length of the bore was ever left open for the river to break into.

questions.stem: The student wants to explain why the grain size of the imported sand matters. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
  • A nourishment scheme places sand dredged offshore onto an eroding beach.
  • The sand placed may be coarser or finer than the sand already there, depending on where it was dredged.
  • Waves carry finer sand offshore again within a season or two.
  • One beach given sand coarser than its own held its width for eleven years.
  • Nourishment does nothing to stop the process that removed the sand in the first place.

choices.label: A
choices.content: A nourishment scheme places sand dredged offshore onto an eroding beach.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Nourishment does nothing to stop the process that removed the sand in the first place.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The sand placed may be coarser or finer than the sand already there, depending on where it was dredged.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Because waves carry fine sand offshore within a season or two while a beach given coarser sand held its width for eleven years, the size of the imported grains decides how long the work lasts.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

The machine's real advantage is thus not speed alone but the _____ of excavation and support.

questions.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “resolve” most nearly mean?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: A bat hunting among foliage must separate the echo of a moth from the echoes of the leaves behind it, and the two return only a fraction of a millisecond apart. Species that hunt in dense cover emit very short calls of wide bandwidth, because a short call can <u>resolve</u> two echoes that a long one runs together. The cost is that a short call carries little energy and cannot be heard far away.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To make a firm decision about a course of action.

choices.label: C
choices.content: To break something down into simpler parts.

choices.label: C

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: The late Roman army in the east was paid in coin raised by taxation and quartered wherever it was needed. From the seventh century, with the wealthiest eastern provinces lost and the treasury much reduced, soldiers were instead settled on land in the provinces and drew their maintenance from it, serving when called. The districts so organised took their names from the units stationed in them, and their commanders came to hold civil as well as military authority.

choices.label: A
choices.content: To describe a change in how an army was supported and what that change did to provincial government.

choices.label: B
choices.content: To argue that the seventh-century army was more effective than its predecessor.

choices.content: To explain how taxes were assessed in the late Roman provinces.

questions.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

questions.passage: A stretch of coast can often be treated as a closed compartment: sand enters it from a river mouth or an eroding cliff, travels along it under the waves, and leaves it down a submarine canyon at the far end. Within such a compartment a loss at one place is usually a gain at another. Armouring a cliff protects the houses on top of it and at the same time cuts off the supply that fed the beaches downdrift, where the deficit appears some years later.

choices.label: A
choices.content: It traces the history of coastal engineering in a single region.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It disputes the claim that sand travels along a coast.

choices.label: C
choices.content: It sets out a way of accounting for sand along a coast and then applies it to a particular intervention.

choices.label: D

questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: In several desert ant species certain workers never leave the nest. Nestmates feed them until the crop swells the abdomen to the size of a grape and the animal can no longer walk; it hangs from the ceiling of a deep chamber for months at a time. When forage fails, a worker strokes one of these swollen individuals and receives a drop of the stored liquid. The colony has in effect turned a run of good weeks into a store that neither dries out nor is carried off by others.

choices.label: A
choices.content: Ant colonies in deserts are smaller than those in wetter regions.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Certain ants serve their colonies as living containers holding a surplus against lean periods.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Desert ants avoid foraging during the hottest part of the year.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Ants that can no longer walk are removed from the nest by their nestmates.

questions.stem: According to the text, what makes the wanted mineral rise in a flotation cell?
questions.subject: READING_WRITING
questions.passage: Most metal ores contain a few per cent of the mineral wanted and a great deal of rock that resembles it. Flotation exploits a difference in wetting: the crushed ore is stirred into water with a reagent that clings to the mineral surface and makes it repel water, and air blown through the pulp carries those particles up in a froth that is skimmed off. The rock, still wetted, sinks. Ore bodies too poor for any earlier method became workable within a decade of the process being introduced.

choices.label: A
choices.content: A reagent makes its surface repel water so that air bubbles carry it up.

choices.label: B
choices.content: It dissolves in the water and is drawn off with the froth.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The stirring throws the finer particles to the surface.

choices.label: D
choices.content: It is lighter than the rock that accompanies it.

choices.label: A
choices.content: The total cost, in dollars, of stringing the whole route

3x+5y=41
5x+3y=39

questions.stem: On a cable ship's plotting sheet a straight course is the set of points \((x,y)\) satisfying \(y=mx+b\), where m and b are constants. The course passes through \((-2,9)\) and \((6,-7)\). What is the value of \(m+b\)?

questions.stem: A boiler shop rivets seams in two patterns. Four metres of the double-riveted pattern together with seven metres of the single-riveted pattern take 63 rivets, while seven metres of the double-riveted pattern together with four metres of the single-riveted pattern take 69 rivets. How many rivets does one metre of the double-riveted pattern take?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A telegraph company's charge for a new line is \(C(n)=an+b\) dollars for a line n miles long, where a and b are constants. A 30-mile line costs $1,290 and a 50-mile line costs $2,050. Which expression gives the charge, in dollars, for a line m miles long?
questions.subject: MATH

questions.stem: A cable ship pays out cable at a steady rate. Three hours after paying out began, 8.4 nautical miles of cable remained on the drum; seven hours after it began, 5.2 nautical miles remained. The ship must leave at least 1.2 nautical miles on the drum. For how many further hours after the seventh hour can the ship go on paying out?
questions.subject: MATH
